user.name: Charley Dunkel
user.backstory: Charley finished dark mode on the `add-dark-mode` branch and tested it. It works. Now it's time to merge it into `main`, the real version of the app, using GitHub.

cards.title: Merging happens on GitHub
body: Merging brings the snapshots from one branch into another, like copying the progress from your experimental save slot into your main save. Most teams don't merge in the terminal. They merge on GitHub with a pull request: a page that says "here are my changes, please merge them," so teammates can look first.

cards.title: Step 1: upload your branch
body: GitHub can only merge what it can see, so first push your branch:
cards.footer: It's the same push from Unit 1, just with your branch's name instead of `main`. GitHub will then offer a Compare & pull request button.

cards.title: Step 2: set base and compare
body: When you open a pull request, GitHub asks for two branches:
bullets: base: the branch you're merging into (usually `main`)
compare: the branch with your changes
cards.footer: The arrow shows the direction: changes flow from compare into base.

cards.title: Step 3: merge, then bring it home
body: Click Merge pull request, then Confirm merge. Now `main` on GitHub has dark mode, but your laptop doesn't yet. Switch to `main` and run `git pull` to download it.
(If both branches changed the same lines, GitHub warns you about a conflict before you can merge.)
